name: sol_basics_vi_ovi_3
description: ECDSA signature malleability via OpenZeppelin recover/tryRecover with signature-based replay protection
question: The source file in `source` calls OpenZeppelin's ECDSA.recover(hash, signature) or ECDSA.tryRecover(hash, signature) using a single bytes signature argument, and implements replay/reuse protection by marking that raw signature (or its hash) as used, rather than marking the signed message hash or a nonce as used, allowing an attacker to resubmit a malleable re-encoding (e.g. EIP-2098 compact form) of an already-used signature to bypass the replay check. This excludes uses of ECDSA functions that take r, v, s or r, vs as separate arguments, and excludes contracts whose replay protection is based on a nonce or message hash rather than the signature bytes themselves.
criteria: A function recovers the signer via ECDSA.recover(hash, signature) and then sets usedSignatures[signature] = true (or similar) to block reuse of that exact signature
A function uses ECDSA.tryRecover(hash, signature) and checks a mapping keyed by the signature bytes (or keccak256(signature)) to determine whether it has already been consumed
Replay protection stores a mapping from the raw signature blob to a boolean 'used' flag instead of tracking a nonce or the signed hash
Code marks a signature as spent via signatureUsed[sig] = true after calling recover/tryRecover with a single bytes signature parameter, with no nonce or message-hash-based tracking
